newsitem.title: USA: U.S. attacks Iraq with cruise missiles.
newsitem.headline: U.S. attacks Iraq with cruise missiles.

text.p: The U.S. military on Tuesday launched cruise missile strikes against air defense targets in Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds, the Pentagon said.
The Defence Department gave no further immediate details.

But U.S. defence officials, who asked not to be identified, said the unmanned and highly-accurate missiles were fired from B-52 bombers and American warships in the Gulf at air defence command and control military targets in and around Baghdad.
The Pentagon said the raids were launched on orders from President Bill Clinton.

"At the direction of the President, the Department of Defence has launched cruise missiles to attack selected air defence targets in Iraq. No further details are available at this time," the brief announcement said.

"The president plans to make a formal statement on this operation at approximately 8 a.m. (1200 GMT) this morning. Shortly after the president makes his statement, the secretary of defence and the vice chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff will hold a press conference" at the Pentagon, it added.
Air raid sirens sounded in parts of Baghdad, but there was no official confirmation in that the U.S. raids had taken place.
State-run radio continued with its normal programmes, and Iraqis on the street said they did not care if an attack were launched.
Official newspapers appearing on Tuesday had no comment on a possible military strike against Iraq.

The United States last sent cruise missiles against Iraq in June 1993 to avenge an alleged plot to kill former U.S. president George Bush during a visit to Kuwait. The attacks then killed six civilians.
